craft_notes: Sthāyin: amṛta-śānta of quenched fever; maṅgala-śānta of pure treatise — the work lands in two breaths (nectar drunk, method pure). Nectar drunk quenches; poison-fever named whole; non-dual told. Rejected: (a) nectar→elixir → killed: nectar is the term. Read aloud: THIS-non-DU-al, THUS-told — KNOW-ledge-NEC-tar PAST com-PARE — … HIS sam-SĀ-ra-POI-son FE-ver.

lines: This non-dual, thus told — knowledge-nectar past compare —
who drinks is quenched: his saṃsāra-poison fever.
l4.sanskrit_cite: etad advayam ity uktaṃ jñānāmṛtam anuttamam | yaḥ pibec chāmyate tasya saṃsāraviṣamūrchanam

reads_against.argmap: Who drinks and is quenched? → Non-dual nectar drunk quenches poison-fever.
